action: Search your GitHub organisations for wfx-docs branches and pull requests titled 'docs: dependency audit notes', and look for gaps in workflow run numbers. Where the payload ran, rotate every secret and cloud role those workflows could reach.
exec: Hijacked developer accounts are being used to plant key-stealing code in software projects, a risk for any team building on GitHub.
plain: Attackers used 4,837 taken-over GitHub accounts to probe more than 61,000 code projects and ran password-stealing code in the build systems of at least 1,835 of them.

key_findings: From about 12:45 UTC on November 10, 4,837 compromised GitHub accounts opened probe pull requests in 61,764 repositories to test for write access.
At least 1,835 repositories ran the payload and had credentials taken; the true figure may be higher because run logs were deleted.
The stealer arrives through an altered workflow, an npm postinstall hook or a throwaway workflow, and is reverted within about a minute.
It takes Actions secrets, cloud and registry credentials and AI provider keys, then pivots into AWS, GCP, Azure, Vault and Kubernetes.
New tricks include forged success status checks, rewritten AWS role trust policies and Azure federated credentials named wfx-ci for persistence.
recommendations: Search for wfx-docs branches and pull requests titled 'docs: dependency audit notes'.
Check for gaps in workflow run numbers, which may be the only trace of a run.
If the payload ran, rotate every secret and cloud role available to that repository's workflows.
Review AWS role trust policies and remove Azure federated credentials named wfx-ci.
Treat machines that installed the affected Packagist or Go module versions as compromised.

summary: Aikido reports that from November 10 an attacker used 4,837 compromised GitHub accounts to open probe pull requests in 61,764 repositories, then ran a secrets-stealing script in the build pipelines of at least 1,835. The script takes pipeline secrets and cloud credentials, pivots into cloud accounts and erases its traces within about a minute. One Packagist package and two Go module versions also carried it.
title: wfx-loot campaign uses 4,837 hijacked GitHub accounts to push secrets-stealing malware

validation.note: Reviewed against the original Aikido Security report.
